constraint_decided_it: E81 Transformation requires 'the simultaneous destruction of one or more than one E18 Physical Thing and the creation of one or more than one E18 Physical Thing', and P124 transformed (E81 -> E18) requires the old item to have 'ceased to exist'. Nothing was destroyed in 1998 -- the frame and cylinders 'had never been touched' -- so there is no destruction leg for the E81 and P124 has no legitimate subject. E80's scope note names the only redirect to E81: 'If the instance of E80 Part Removal results in the total decomposition of the original object into pieces, such that the whole ceases to exist'. Removing one part (the boiler) is not total decomposition. Conversely P46's own scope note, which B cites, prescribes the opposite construct: 'If a component is not part of a whole from the beginning of existence or until the end of existence of the whole, the classes E79 Part Addition and E90 [sic, E80] Part Removal can be used to document when a component became part of a particular whole and/or when it stopped being a part of it.' That is exactly A's model.
better_modelling: A reached it. One continuing E22 Human-Made Object; the wartime scrapping as E80 Part Removal (P112 diminished: the engine, P113 removed: the boiler) plus E6 Destruction (P13 destroyed: the boiler) -- E80's own example is 'the removal of the engine from my car'; the 1998 boiler build as E12 Production (P108 has produced, range E24, satisfied) and its fitting as E79 Part Addition (P110 augmented: the engine, P111 added: the new boiler), with P46 is composed of asserting the new boiler as part of the engine. The fifty dormant years are a phase of the same object, not a gap in its existence -- Velios in t1170 offers exactly this industrial-heritage case ('"not functional" is what we call machines in industrial heritage collections') as an observable property of a phase. E11 Modification would be correct but too general; E79/E80 are its more specific subclasses and are the required choice.
reasoning: Every property A proposes sits inside its declared domain and range (P112/P113 E80->E18, P110/P111 E79->E18, P13 E6->E18, P108 E12->E24), and A checked the one clause that could have forced E81 -- E80's 'total decomposition ... such that the whole ceases to exist' -- and correctly found it unmet. B's E81 fails on the class definition itself: there is no destruction in 1998, so the mandatory destruction leg of E81 and the 'ceased to exist' condition of P124 are both unsatisfied, and B then contradicts itself by carrying the frame across P46 'into both wholes' after asserting via P124 that one whole ceased to exist. B's appeal to Doerr's warehouse variant in t1170 misreads it: there 'each of the removed pieces were stored in a warehouse' -- the whole was fully disassembled -- whereas Doerr's stated criterion is 'continuity of coherence and functionality' where 'Coherence includes keeping parts together as a functional whole', and this engine's frame and cylinders stayed assembled throughout. All quoted wording in both answers verified verbatim (t1170 msg [10] and [11], E24, E81, E11's Enola Gay E12+E81 example), so neither is unsupported; A additionally and correctly noted that Issue 369's outcome text only transfers the Phase discussion to Issue 422 and does not ratify Doerr's E19-identity remarks as a SIG ruling. B's t1265, t1396 and Monotonicity citations are never used to support any claim in its answer.
